ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The transition-state drawing shows a left aromatic iodolactone-type skeleton with a benzene ring, an iodine center attached to the aryl system, an O-containing lactone carbonyl unit, and three acetate-type AcO/OAc ligands around iodine. Curved arrows are drawn but are to be ignored. On the right, there is an alcohol/alkyl fragment with an oxygen bearing H and attached to a carbon substituted by R1 and R2. Counting excluding all bonds to hydrogen: For the left aryl-iodolactone skeleton, count 6 bonds around the benzene ring, 1 aryl–I bond, 1 aryl–carbonyl-carbon bond, 1 carbonyl C=O bond, 1 carbonyl C–O bond, and 1 O–I bond, for 11 bonds. For the three AcO/OAc ligands, each acetate ligand contributes 3 internal heavy-atom bonds plus 1 I–O attachment, so 3 × 4 = 12 bonds. For the right-hand alcohol/alkyl fragment, exclude O–H and count O–C, C–R1, and C–R2, for 3 bonds. Total = 11 + 12 + 3 = 26.

method.method_draft: Describe the image first, then partition the structure into fragments. Count the left aryl-iodolactone skeleton: 6 bonds around the benzene ring, 1 aryl–I bond, 1 aryl–carbonyl-carbon bond, 1 carbonyl C=O bond, 1 carbonyl C–O bond, and 1 O–I bond, giving 11. Count the three AcO/OAc ligands: each contributes 3 internal heavy-atom bonds plus 1 I–O attachment, so 3 × 4 = 12. Count the right-hand alcohol/alkyl fragment excluding O–H: O–C, C–R1, and C–R2, giving 3. Add 11 + 12 + 3 = 26.

method.method_draft: After describing the visual structure, make a heavy-atom graph. Assign degrees: the six aryl carbons contribute 14 total degrees because four have degree 2, one is bonded to iodine, and one is bonded to the carbonyl carbon; the lactone carbonyl carbon, carbonyl oxygen, and lactone oxygen contribute 3 + 1 + 2; iodine has degree 5 to aryl carbon, lactone oxygen, and three acetoxy oxygens; the three acetoxy groups excluding iodine contribute 3 × 7 = 21 degrees; the right-hand alcohol fragment contributes 6 degrees from central C, O, R1, and R2, with O–H ignored. The total degree sum is 14 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 5 + 21 + 6 = 52, so the bond count is 52/2 = 26.
